title: Candidate feedback draft - Daniel Park (Senior Serving Runtime Engineer)
content:
Candidate: Daniel Park
Role: Senior Serving Runtime Engineer (inference serving/runtime)
Interviewer (this draft): Isabella Chen (acting on notes from panel)
Other interviewers: Ravi Patel (runtime), Maya Thompson (sre)
Date: 2026-03-02

Summary: Daniel is a strong systems candidate with solid low-level knowledge of GPU inference workflows and a pragmatic approach to trade-offs. He has prior experience building inference pipelines at scale (was on the infra team at a mid-size ML startup). He did well on system-design and operational questions but showed some gaps in advanced optimization/quantization details and in the coding exercise edge cases. Overall leaning +1 (recommend move to final loop / hiring manager sync), pending reference check on recent project delivery.

Breakdown by area (quick notes for scoring):
- Technical depth (GPUs, batching, KV cache): 4/5
  - Explained continuous batching design and how to handle variable seq lengths. Good explanations of memory management for KV cache and multi-tenant isolation strategies.
  - Was less confident on low-level CUDA kernel tuning specifics and some quantization trade-offs (LUTs vs QAT). Understands conceptually but lacks hands-on depth on quantization tooling (e.g., bitsandbytes internals).

- System design (throughput/latency/routing): 4/5
  - Clean design for request routing with policy-based fallbacks (latency vs cost). Good on autoscaling strategy that accounts for burst capacity and warm-up time for model weights.
  - Thoughtful about graceful degradation (fall back to cheaper model variants) and cache priming. Could have been more explicit about backpressure mechanisms between batching service and GPU pools.

- Coding (algorithms + implementation): 3/5
  - Coding exercise (streaming token aggregator) produced a correct high-level approach. Implementation had a couple of edge-case bugs (concurrency on buffer flush, off-by-one in sequence join). Reasonable debugging approach when prompted.
  - Would expect stronger test coverage habits and more defensive concurrency handling for production code.

- Reliability & SRE mindset: 4/5
  - Strong on observability: advocated for route-level latency histograms, token-level cost metrics, and KL-based regression alerts. Familiar with tracing and correlating traces with per-token cost.
  - Incident handling experience OK; described a postmortem where a bad model rollout caused increased latency and how they rolled back and implemented circuit breakers.

- Culture & communication: 4/5
  - Clear communicator, pragmatic, collaborative. Asked good clarifying questions during design discussion. Seemed excited about ownership and mentoring.

Risks / open questions:
- Quantization depth: candidate knows conceptual trade-offs but hasn't shipped aggressive quantization (4-bit/INT4) in production; would need pairing or guidance on vendor/tooling specifics for aggressive compression.
- Concurrency correctness: coding exercise revealed some threading/race issues under stress — may need to probe further in a follow-up or include a short take-home test focused on concurrency.
- Compensation expectations: asked for target range that is in-line with our Sr. level band (confirmed via recruiter).

Recommendation: Proceed to final loop with hiring manager and one additional deep-dive on quantization/low-level optimization (can be a short technical chat with Ravi). If hiring manager agrees, move to verbal offer pending references.

Suggested next steps:
1) Schedule 30m follow-up with Ravi focusing on quantization and kernel trade-offs (practical questions + past project deep-dive).
2) Quick take-home or pair-debug session (45m) to validate concurrency/edge-case handling from coding exercise, or have a focused question set during the follow-up.
3) Check references on most recent infra project (JIRA-ENG-1423 referenced).

Scorecard (panel aggregation):
- technical: 4
- system_design: 4
- coding: 3
- reliability: 4
- communication: 4

Notes to self (Isabella):
- Keep feedback concise for panel sync doc. Highlight positive ops/SRE instincts and note quantization knowledge gap as coachable.
- Prepare 5 specific quantization questions for Ravi to use in follow-up (e.g., experience with QAT vs PTQ, fallback strategies when quantized model degrades, perf profiling tools used).
- Add candidate to candidate-tracking sheet and mark status = "final-loop-scheduled" once follow-up confirmed.

Draft email blurb for recruiter (short):
"Daniel had a strong interview with the serving/runtime panel. We recommend a final technical follow-up on quantization and a short concurrency validation session before proceeding to an offer. Candidate aligns with Sr. band — please confirm references and availability for a 30m follow-up with Ravi this week."
